questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good film programme, an interesting destination, and having formerly studied at a high school in New Zealand

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation week was fine, felt a little bit condescending and childish at times, but I suppose some people need more support when abroad than I did.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Stayed in a house near campus, don't know if that counts as campus housing

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very random who you end up with and they may end up becoming your best friend but it can also feel a little antisocial compared to at least Danish dorms. Oh and the house was a bit neglected and cold. But overall, it was fine. Nothing awful, just nothing amazing either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Don't really recall the exact process at this point. I know there were a bunch of registration forms and I had to go get my passport and other documents verified by a lawyer and the Danish ministry of foreign affairs, which is fine I guess, since I live in Copenhagen, but it's a lot of paperwork. Which makes sense of course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got exactly the ones I asked for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions and it's pretty straightforward.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had one course that I was very impressed with - current issues in film studies. The other two were all right, but the level seemed kind of low compared to UCPH. Very interesting topics though.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lower than Copenhagen standards for the 100 and 200 level courses I took. However, the 300 level course, current issues in film studies, was super interesting, and the level was higher (again, makes sense). I was very impressed with that course and its teacher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Slightly different. I haven't had tutorials at UCPH before, where the course is divided into smaller groups and we do little assignments. It seemed a little high school-y to me. Also, the amount of assignments was way higher than in Copenhagen. I had one every few weeks and with 3 courses at once that made for a lot of writing assignments and not a lot of time to actually study the subject.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Current issues in film studies, gender and genre, and Mental Health and Disorder: Inter-disciplinary Perspectives

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Current issues in film studies - or any courses taught by Dr Tim Groves for that matter.

questions.answer: None, as I recall.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent and groceries. They were about the same as Copenhagen prices which surprised me. Especially because the housing is as sad as it is, I am surprised they charge the same as Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A LOT. All sorts of sport clubs, language clubs, film clubs, cultural clubs, poetry, music... you name it, they had a club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did a lot of hiking and travelling around the rest of the country, which I highly recommend.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking and travelling.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, I think. It's different from Denmark, for sure, but the kiwis are a very welcoming people and want to help out where they can. It is a more sociable culture, where it is common to talk to people you don't know at pubs or other places in public. Colonization means that they have very European sensibilities and it doesn't feel that far from home. Meanwhile, Maori culture is super interesting and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and friendly. Try and talk to people, they're not as closed off as Danes are. Go out and have some beers with people, if you drink. Or join one of the many many clubs as a way to meet people over a common interest.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I had to overcome my instinct of not talking to strangers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their humour, their openness, and of course the Maori culture which is so different from any European culture and something I think we can learn a lot from.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open to new experiences, get out of the flat and see what the city and the rest of the country has to offer, and make friends and make plans, because before you know it, you're out of time and headed back home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think I rediscovered my love for film studies thanks to the course Current issues in film studies and Tim Groves' teaching. I was so impressed and interested in that course.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Staying active and interested after a few months when the novelty had worn off.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
